title: ID0461823-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Control-layer failure on Connector 2
description:
Reported Behaviour/ Issue: Control-layer failure on Connector 2
Solution: Customer started a transaction in DC1 while plug-in DC2, also backend sent a reboot -> Not charger problem, check with backend and inform the customer how to use the app.

additional_info.subject: Roaming authorisations repeatedly rejected - causing failure
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco / Siemens Support,
We need to escalate a stability issue that occurred at Galway Retail Park on
13 November
, the day after the firmware patch was applied to address the control-layer failure on Connector 2.
Please review the following sequence from the GreenFlux logs between
13:04:06 and 13:09:24
on Charger
170003301
:
Roaming authorisations repeatedly rejected (Hubject Invalid)
TokenResponse:
"Unsuccessful authentication via hubject: Invalid"
These attempts did not start sessions, but indicate repeated failed authentication attempts on a normally stable connector.
Immediate charger-side failure events
The unit then entered an error state and triggered a
PerformingCollaboratedReboot
:
VendorErrorCode:
"PerformingCollaboratedReboot"
Status:
Unavailable /
Error
This reboot was not remotely initiated by us or GreenFlux.
Main breaker fault message
Immediately after this reboot, the charger reported:
VendorErrorCode:
"Mainbreaker_QA1"
Status:
Unavailable /
Error
This implies the unit tripped its main breaker or detected an internal condition that required the breaker to be opened.
SECC re-initialisation error
Once the reboot completed, the SECC reported:
VendorErrorCode:
"secc is initializing"
ConnectorStatus:
Unavailable
The entire system remained Unavailable until the SECC recovered.
To be clear, this is
not
the same behaviour as the 10 November incident (which involved the charger continuing to deliver energy after the backend session had stopped). On 13 November, the charger instead fell into a full error state, dropped offline, rebooted, and temporarily disabled all four connectors.
However, both issues appear to originate from the same control-layer / SECC integration zone that the firmware patch was intended to stabilise.
Given this, we require Siemens to review:
Is a collaborated reboot with a Mainbreaker_QA1 fault expected behaviour after the firmware update?
If this is normal during the first stabilisation cycle post-update, please confirm formally.
If not expected, does this sequence indicate an ongoing instability in the SECC ↔ main controller communication layer?
The pattern—reboot, main breaker event, SECC re-initialisation—suggests a deeper system-level issue.
Is further firmware or on-site diagnostic work planned or required?
We need Siemens to confirm whether this was a one-off recovery behaviour or whether it represents something that requires investigation.
Impact on site operations
UCC (GreenFlux’s contractor) escalated to us because all four connectors were reported unavailable by a customer, and the unit required manual attention. Please treat this as an operational-impact incident.
Given that this occurred the day after the firmware fix for the control-layer charging fault, we need to be certain the system is stable and that no residual risk exists of either:
• uncontrolled energy flow (10 November issue), or
• spontaneous system shutdowns (13 November issue).
Please acknowledge and provide Siemens’ assessment of the logs above, and confirm whether any additional corrective actions are required.
Regards,
Colin Barry

additional_info.subject: ID0461823-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Control-layer failure on Connector 2 CRM:03055000346
additional_info.body:
Hello Colin,
Thanks for reporting this.
I checked the logs and here is what I find:
1. At 12:54 customer plugged-in connector 2:
When authentication was requested:
And here is the Remote Authentication:
He started a transaction for
connector 1
and not connector 2. Which is still accepted, but from the top log you can see that the charger is reporting back "there is no cable connected"
30 seconds later, the customer must've thought, ok why is my charging not starting? And tried again the same authentication for the same
connector 1
.
Here, the OCPP backend is conveying back to us, I already have started a session for this connector 30 secs ago, so I do not allow a new session to be created until the first one is cleared or finished.
These attempts all failed since they chose the wrong connector.
2. Regarding the reboot, I see that someone from the backend performed the reboot:
So you need to check with your backend who did it.
Regarding your questions:
Is a collaborated reboot with a Mainbreaker_QA1 fault expected behaviour after the firmware update?
This is normal in any version of the SiD, when you do a reboot, we must open the Mainbreaker to unsure we are according to safety norms
If not expected, does this sequence indicate an ongoing instability in the SECC ↔ main controller communication layer?
This is not related to SECC
Is further firmware or on-site diagnostic work planned or required?
No since the problem seems to be user and backend generated
Impact on site operations
Since the charger performed a reboot, then the outlets are unavailable until the boot up is fully finished.
Please let me know if I answered all your questions. Since the problem is not charger related, I will wait for your feedback.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
